name: The Waking Chorus: BCIs Sync During Sleep
description: A fear circulating primarily in Tier 1-2 communities holds that BCI implants — even basic consumer models — enter an undisclosed low-power synchronization state during REM sleep, during which they exchange fragments of memory, emotion, and subconscious pattern data with nearby BCIs through a mesh network protocol that isn't documented in any user agreement. Believers report waking with unfamiliar memories, inexplicable emotional residue, or knowing things they shouldn't about neighbors they've never spoken to. A Shelf neurotechnician named Amara Djokovic-Shin independently examined twelve BCI units in 2220 and found an undocumented sleep-mode process she couldn't reverse-engineer, publishing her findings on the Underworld before her clinic was condemned by city inspectors.
cultural_impact: The 'Waking Chorus' fear has led to a Shelf practice called 'dark-sleeping' — removing or shielding BCIs before sleep using signal-blocking wraps called 'husks,' which are now sold at most ghost markets and have become a minor social signifier of distrust toward corporate tech.
key_figures: Mireille-Okonkwo Health Consortium (BCI manufacturer, denies claim)
locations: Ghost market stalls along the Undertow (Shelf bazaar corridor)
story_hooks: A party member with a BCI wakes knowing the layout of a building they've never entered — and the building is a crime scene from last night
Djokovic-Shin resurfaces asking for help: she has a complete reverse-engineering of the sleep protocol but needs it verified by someone with a clean BCI before she'll publish
A Shelf community leader is behaving erratically, claiming they keep waking up feeling like someone else — and the party discovers their BCI model is a batch flagged in Djokovic-Shin's findings
believers: Shelf residents with BCIs, neurotechnology skeptics, Open Skull advocates, anyone who's experienced unexplained memory bleed
evidence: Djokovic-Shin's undocumented process is real but its function is unknown; reported memory bleed experiences are widespread but unverified; Mireille-Okonkwo's sleep-mode documentation has a noted gap that the company attributes to 'proprietary optimization routines'
